The Techiman North District Assembly has inaugurated 58 sanitation guards tasked with keeping the district clean and healthy, in a move to tackle poor sanitation and youth unemployment simultaneously.
The newly recruited environmental guards were officially outdoored at a brief ceremony held at the Assembly premises in Tuobodom, marking a significant step in the district's resolve to improve sanitation standards while creating employment opportunities for the teeming unemployed youth.
Addressing the gathering, the District Chief Executive (DCE) for Techiman North, Hon. Adom Kwabena Johnson, explained that the initiative serves two critical purposes.
"This move will not only help improve the sanitation situation in our district but will also augment the government's monthly cleanup exercises," the DCE stated.
"We believe that by empowering our youth to take charge of their environment, we are building a healthier and more prosperous district."
The DCE emphasized that the Assembly is committed to ensuring the guards work under safe and dignified conditions. To this end, he announced that the Assembly had procured adequate Personal Protective Equipment (PPEs) to aid their work.
The equipment provided to the sanitation guards includes hand gloves, nose masks, reflective jackets, Wellington boots, wheelbarrows, rakes, shovels, and brooms. In a significant boost to waste management efforts, the Assembly also procured two tricycles specifically for the evacuation of refuse after cleanups.
"This is a complete package," the DCE noted. "We are not just giving them jobs; we are giving them the tools they need to do those jobs effectively and safely."
Hon. Johnson also used the occasion to appeal to residents to cooperate with the environmental guards, urging them to see the new recruits as partners in progress rather than intruders.
"I urge all residents to cooperate with the environmental guards who are here to help with sanitation services. Let us support them, encourage them, and work together to make Techiman North the cleanest district in the region," he added.
The District Environmental Officer, Mr. Anass Baba Iddrisu, could not hide his excitement about the initiative. He expressed confidence that the new workforce would help sanitize the environment entirely.
"This is a dream come true for the environmental department," Mr. Iddrisu said. "For a long time, we have struggled with inadequate personnel to maintain cleanliness across the district. With these 58 guards on board, I am confident that we will see a remarkable transformation in our sanitation standards."
He added that the environmental guards would be deployed to various communities across the district to ensure that waste is properly managed and the environment is kept clean at all times.
For the new recruits, the opportunity represents more than just a job—it is a chance to contribute to their community and secure a livelihood.
Speaking on behalf of her colleagues, Ms. Brako Helena expressed gratitude to the Assembly for the opportunity.
"We are thankful to the authorities for giving us this chance to serve," she said. "We pledge to help keep the environment clean. We will not let the Assembly or the people of Techiman North down."
The recruits, who cut across different communities in the district, will undergo orientation on proper waste management, sanitation practices, and environmental health before being deployed to their various stations.
The Techiman North initiative is being viewed as a model that other districts could adopt. By combining sanitation improvement with job creation, the Assembly is addressing two critical Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)—Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth)—at the local level.
